===== owners.GET.yml =====
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
service:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ListOwners
  govern: [ readonly-transaction ]

===== owners.POST.yml =====
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Validate the body first so a missing or blank required field is a 400 before any
# owner is built or saved. It publishes the body for the build step to reuse.
validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  next: normalizeTelephone

# Strip non-digits from the telephone and require exactly 10 digits, so the owner is
# built and stored with the normalized value and a bad number is a 400.
normalizeTelephone:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerTelephone
  next: normalizeEmail

# The email is optional; when present it must be a valid address (else a 400) and is
# stored and returned lower-cased.
normalizeEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerEmail
  next: rejectDisposableEmail

# When an email is present, reject it as a 400 if its domain is on the disposable-domain
# blocklist. Runs after the email is validated and normalized and before any owner is
# built or saved.
rejectDisposableEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectDisposableEmail
  next: validatePostcode

# The postcode is optional; when present it must be 4 digits and valid for the city's
# region (else a 400), before any owner is built or saved. Stored and returned unchanged.
validatePostcode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerPostcode
  next: validateRegistrationDate

# The registrationDate is optional; when supplied it must not be later than the server's
# current date (else a 400), before any owner is built or saved. Runs before the date is
# resolved and rolled forward to a business day.
validateRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateRegistrationDate
  next: ensureUniqueIdentity

# The duplicate block: reject a request whose (lastName, postcode) household is already
# occupied by an existing owner, as a 409, before any owner is built or saved. A request
# that opts in with 'sharesHousehold' bypasses the block and is created as a declared
# household member.
ensureUniqueIdentity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureUniqueIdentity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureCityCapacity

# Reject a request whose city already holds the maximum number of owners as a 409,
# before any owner is built or saved.
ensureCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: resolveRegistrationDate

# Resolve the effective registration date (supplied, else the server's current date) and
# roll a weekend forward to the next business day. Runs before the daily-limit check so
# the limit counts against the adjusted business day this create will land on.
resolveRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ResolveRegistrationDate
  next: ensureDailyLimit

# Reject a create once the maximum number of owners has already been registered on the
# resolved business day (by registrationDate) as a 429, before any owner is built or saved.
ensureDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: applyRegistrationDate

# Stamp the built owner with the resolved business-day registration date, overwriting any
# date the request body mapped in, so the owner is stored and returned with the adjusted day.
applyRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ApplyRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

# Assign the '<REGION>-<HASH8>' customer code, where REGION is the owner's postcode-derived
# region and HASH8 the first 8 upper-case hex chars of SHA-256(normalizedTelephone + lastName).
# Runs after the telephone is normalized and before save, so the code is stored and returned.
assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignMembershipNumber

# Assign the '<customerCode>-M<YY>' membership number, where YY is the last two digits
# of the registration date year. Runs after the customer code and registration date are
# set and before save, so the number is stored and returned with the owner.
assignMembershipNumber:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignMembershipNumber
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

# Stamp the new owner with its deterministic 'householdId' (first 12 hex of SHA-256 over
# its normalized last name and postcode), so owners with the same last name and postcode
# share it automatically. Runs before save so the id is stored and returned with the owner.
assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHouseholdSize

# Record the household's size after this create (members sharing the householdId plus the
# new owner), so the responder can promote a 3+ member household to the GOLD tier. Runs
# after the householdId is assigned and before save, so the size is stored with the owner.
assignHouseholdSize:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHouseholdSize
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: countNamesakes

# Record how many existing owners already share this owner's first and last name
# (case-insensitively). Runs before save so the count excludes the new owner and is
# stored and returned with it.
countNamesakes:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: flagPossibleDuplicate

# Flag a soft duplicate: when an existing owner shares this new owner's last name and
# postcode but has a different telephone, stamp 'possibleDuplicate' true and
# 'possibleDuplicateOf' with the matching owner id. A declared household member
# ('sharesHousehold') is never flagged. Runs before save so the new owner is not yet
# persisted and cannot match itself, and the flag is stored and returned with it.
flagPossibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

# The save assigns the generated id, so audit here to log the created owner's id,
# customerCode and registrationDate to the AUDIT logger before responding.
audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The owner's honorific title. Optional; one of MR, MRS, MS or DR. Stored and returned, and used to compose the salutation.
          type: string
          example: DR
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner. May be supplied directly (flat form, kept for backward compatibility) or composed from the structured 'addressLine1'/'addressLine2' fields when those are present. Normalized (upper-cased, whitespace collapsed, street-type abbreviations expanded) and, in the structured form, returned as the normalized 'addressLine1' with a single space and the normalized 'addressLine2' appended when present.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: The first line of the structured postal address. Optional; preferred over the flat 'address' when a non-blank value is present. Normalized like 'address'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: The optional second line of the structured postal address. Normalized like 'address' and appended to the composed 'address' after a single space when present.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apartment 4B'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: The owner's postcode. Optional; when present it must be exactly 4 digits and, for a city with a known region (Sydney->NSW 2000-2099, Melbourne->VIC 3000-3099, Brisbane->QLD 4000-4099), fall within that region's range. A city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and returned unchanged.
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
          example: '2000'
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. Accepts spaces, dashes and brackets on input; a leading '+' and country code are kept, otherwise Australian country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped. Stored and returned in E.164 form (a leading '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Optional on create; defaults to the server's current date when omitted. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: The owner's date of birth. Optional; when present the owner's ageBand is derived from it. Accepted and returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: When true, allow creating this owner even though another owner already occupies the same household (same last name and postcode) that would otherwise be rejected as a duplicate; the owner is created as a declared household member and is not flagged as a possible duplicate. Write-only; not stored or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            salutation:
              title: Salutation
              description: The owner's salutation, derived on read - the title and last name separated by a single space (e.g. 'DR Franklin'), or just the last name when no title is present.
              type: string
              example: DR Franklin
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: Franklin, George
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: G.F.
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: The owner's canonical region, the REGION segment of its customerCode. Derived from the postcode (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099), falling back to the city-to-region table (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), or 'UNKNOWN'.
              type: string
              example: NSW
              readOnly: true
            timezone:
              title: Timezone
              description: The owner's IANA timezone name, derived from its locality via the pinned region-to-timezone table (NSW->Australia/Sydney, VIC->Australia/Melbourne, QLD->Australia/Brisbane). Null when the locality has no entry.
              type: string
              example: Australia/Sydney
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: The owner's customer code, formatted '<REGION>-<HASH8>' where REGION is the owner's region and HASH8 is the first 8 upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over the normalized telephone concatenated with lastName.
              type: string
              example: NSW-1A2B3C4D
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where YY is the last two digits of the registration date year.
              type: string
              example: NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: The Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits of the owner's customerCode.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 4
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: A deterministic shared identifier for the owner's household, the first 12 hex characters of SHA-256 over the normalized last name and postcode. Owners with the same last name and postcode share it automatically; null for owners without a postcode.
              type: string
              example: 3f2504e04f89
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: The owner's derived identity, formatted 'normalizedTelephone|email|householdId' (email and householdId contribute an empty segment when absent). Duplicate detection itself keys off the householdId (the household is rejected as a duplicate when already occupied, unless the create sets 'sharesHousehold').
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678||3f2504e04f89'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: The number of existing owners who shared this owner's first and last name (compared case-insensitively) at the time this owner was created.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: The owner's membership points. Starts at 0, plus 2 when an email is present, plus 1 when namesakeCount is 0, plus 2 for a household of 3 or more, plus 3 when tenure exceeds 365 days.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: The owner's membership level from 1 to 4, derived from membershipPoints - level 1 (0-1 points), 2 (2-3), 3 (4-5), 4 (6 or more).
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 2
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: True when more than 80 owners have already been registered for the current business day, flagging unusually high daily signup volume; otherwise false.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicate:
              title: Possible duplicate
              description: True when this owner is not a hard duplicate but shares an existing owner's lastName and postcode while having a different telephone; otherwise false.
              type: boolean

## Summary

Changed owner deletion from a hard delete to a soft delete, keeping each concern in its natural home:

- **`model/Owner.java`** — added a `deleted` field (`@Column(name = "deleted")`) initialized to `Boolean.FALSE`, plus getter/setter. The field initializer is what makes a newly created owner serialize `deleted: false` (the insert writes `false` rather than `NULL`).
- **`rest/function/owner/DeleteOwner.java`** — now flags the loaded owner `deleted=true` and `save`s it (was `repository.delete(owner)`). The DELETE pipeline is otherwise unchanged, so it still responds `204` (2xx) and the row is retained; `GET /api/owners/{id}` still loads it by id and returns `deleted: true`.
- **`rest/function/owner/EnsureUniqueIdentity.java`** (the blocking identity check) and **`AssignPossibleDuplicate.java`** (the soft duplicate check) — each now skips owners flagged deleted while scanning existing owners, so a normally-blocking household collision is allowed when the only match has been soft-deleted.
- **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `deleted` boolean to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and MapStruct auto-maps `Owner.getDeleted()` → `OwnerDto.deleted`.
- **`db/hsqldb/schema.sql`** and **`db/h2/schema.sql`** (the test and main profiles) — added `deleted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE` to the `owners` table.

I scoped the exclusion precisely to the create endpoint's duplicate/identity checks (as the spec requires), leaving `findById` — and therefore GET and the delete flow — returning soft-deleted owners untouched. Inactive `jpa`/`jdbc` repository profiles were left alone since they aren't wired in for the app or tests.
